title: Zoom in: the query router reads the coarsest tier that answers the question
caption: The range and the step pick the tier; the still-open part of the range is stitched in from the finer tier.

steps.text: Parse the request: last 7 days, one point per hour, for one campaign.
7 days fits the hour tier: the coarsest tier whose step is no bigger than the one asked for.
Read one row per ad per hour: a few hundred rows instead of millions of raw events.
The range ends at 'now', and the current hour has no hour row yet: add it up from its minute rows.
Return one series; the client can't tell which points came from which tier.

scenarios.name: Live 1-hour panel
scenarios.summary: A short range at fine resolution reads minute rows directly; the newest minute is still open and is marked partial.

steps.text: Last hour, one point per minute.
The current minute's window hasn't closed; return it flagged 'partial' instead of a misleading dip.

scenarios.name: Past retention
scenarios.summary: Minute-level data from 5 months ago was deleted after 30 days. Serve the finest tier that still exists, and say so.

steps.text: Asked: per-minute clicks for a day in June.
Minute rows for that day are gone; fall back to hour rows and tell the client the step became 1 h.
Old range, so nothing to stitch.

scenarios.name: Hour rollup lagging
scenarios.summary: The job that builds hour rows from minute rows is behind. Fill the missing hours from minutes: correct, just more rows read.

steps.text: The hour tier stops 3 hours short of now: its builder is lagging.
Stitch the missing 3 hours from minute rows (180 per ad instead of 3) and raise a freshness alert.
The answer is the same; only the query got more expensive.
